Title: Five immigration officers remanded over alleged role in MyIMMs hacking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Five Immigration Department officers have been remanded until Aug 6 to assist investigations into their alleged involvement in the hacking of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs), linked to the unlawful processing and approval of Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS).
Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order against the four men and one woman, aged between their 30s and 40s, at the Putrajaya Magistrate's Court today following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).S

Title: Former plantation manager held over RM8m rubber seedling contracts probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested a former plantation manager of a rubber seedling supplier in the Klang Valley over alleged misappropriation involving contracts worth about RM8 million.
The man, in his 50s, is being investigated over allegations of abusing contracts for the supply of rubber seedlings to subsidiaries of a statutory body involved in the plantation sector.
According to an MACC source, the suspect was arrested at about 7pm yesterday after he turned up at the MACC headquarters to have his statement recorded.

Title: MACC nabs director in RM300,000 Tabung Haji bribery probes
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has arrested a company director for allegedly bribing a former chief operating officer (COO) of a statutory body with renovation works worth about RM300,000 in return for securing renovation contracts.
The arrest followed investigations by a special task force set up to review the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Tabung Haji. The RCI report was made public on July 29 through the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim)'s official portal.
An MACC source said the suspect, a man in his 50s and director of a design company, was arrested at 7.30pm yesterday after turning up at the MACC headquarters to have his statement recorded.

Title: Building facade collapses in Penang, two injured
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Two people are believed to have been injured after the facade of a building along Lebuh Armenian here collapsed on them.
The incident occurred at about 1pm.
They were rushed to the nearest hospital for treatment.
The New Straits Times has reached out to Penang Island City Council mayor Datuk A. Rajendran for comment.
Lebuh Armenian is a narrow street in George Town, located within the city's Unesco World Heritage Site.
Renowned for its vibrant cultural heritage and captivating street art, it has become one of George Town's most popular attractions.
Lebuh Armenian also holds historical significance as the venue of Sun Yat-sen's Penang Conference, an important event that contributed to the overthrow of the Qing Empire in 1911.
Today, the street is best known for Ernest Zacharevic's iconic Children on a Bicycle mural, alongside numerous other street art installations, traditional Chinese clan houses, museums and heritage shophouses offering antiques, handicrafts and local souvenirs.

Title: Oil giant Aramco's profits soar 44 pct as war boosts prices
Article:
RIYADH: Saudi Aramco on Tuesday said its net profit rose 44 per cent in the second quarter year-on-year as the Middle East war pushed oil and gas prices higher.
Aramco, majority-owned by the state, reported net income of 122.6 billion Saudi riyals ($32.7 billion) from April to June, up from 85 billion riyals ($22.67 billion) in 2025.
Crude prices have been volatile throughout the war and were far higher in the second quarter of 2026 compared with a year earlier.
"Despite the unprecedented supply disruption through the Strait of Hormuz, we continued to demonstrate our ability to maintain business continuity," Aramco president and CEO Amin H. Nasser said in a statement.
He cited Aramco's "diverse asset base and multi-decade planning, including strategic infrastructure such as the East-West Pipeline, storage capacity, and export terminals."
Fighting in the Gulf continues to restrict the passage of hydrocarbons through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, while Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen announced a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea last month.
Stripping out exceptional items, adjusted net income came in at 125.1 billion Saudi riyals ($33.4 billion).
The median analyst consensus for the second quarter adjusted net income was $31.16 billion – an external estimate based on 12 forecasts.

Title: Inflation back in focus as energy prices reshape market outlook, says JustMarkets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Inflation has re-emerged as a key driver of global financial markets in 2026 as higher energy prices, uncertain central bank policy and slowing economic growth reshape investor expectations, trading platform JustMarkets said.
The firm said upcoming consumer price index (CPI) data will be closely watched as markets gauge the outlook for interest rates, currencies, bond yields and risk assets.
Rising oil, natural gas and fuel prices are feeding through to transportation, manufacturing and logistics costs, increasing the likelihood that businesses will pass higher expenses on to consumers, said a company representative.
"With inflation making a strong comeback driven by energy prices, traders must remain vigilant. The upcoming CPI releases are critical catalysts that will dictate market volatility and central bank policies," he said.
The company noted that stronger-than-expected inflation readings typically reinforce expectations of higher interest rates, supporting the US dollar and government bond yields while weighing on equities.
Conversely, weaker inflation data could strengthen expectations for monetary easing, lifting investor sentiment and supporting risk assets.
JustMarkets said financial markets remain in a delicate position as persistent inflation coincides with uneven economic growth, complicating the policy outlook for major central banks.
It said foreign exchange markets, particularly major currency pairs such as EUR/USD, GBP/USD and USD/JPY, are among the most sensitive to CPI releases.
Gold prices also tend to react sharply to changes in inflation expectations, real interest rates and movements in the US dollar, while equity indices and commodities respond to shifts in borrowing costs and inflation expectations.
The firm said traders typically prepare for CPI releases by reviewing economic forecasts, assessing existing positions and managing portfolio risk, as inflation data often triggers heightened market volatility, wider trading spreads and sharp price swings.
Despite a period of easing price pressures in recent years, JustMarkets said inflation has regained importance in shaping market direction, with energy costs, monetary policy uncertainty and slowing growth expected to keep CPI data at the centre of investor attention.

Title: MCW urges focus on KLIA security lapses in pilot drug probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Corruption Watch (MCW) has called for investigations into the arrest of a pilot found with drugs in Indonesia to focus on potential weaknesses in security systems at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), rather than solely identifying which agency was responsible.
Its president, Jais Abdul Karim, said the statement by the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) that the pilot had cleared all security checks at KLIA, while baggage screening fell under Aviation Security (AVSEC), should be viewed in its entirety.
"The real issue is how such a large quantity of drugs could allegedly pass through the security system of an international airport.
"If all procedures were followed but the threat still went undetected, then those procedures must be comprehensively reviewed.
"The focus of the investigation should not be limited to determining which agency was responsible, but whether there were systemic weaknesses that need to be addressed," he said in a statement today.
He said the team set up by the Transport Ministry should determine whether the incident was caused by technological shortcomings, human negligence or organised criminal activity.
At the same time, he urged the public to refrain from speculating about the airline or individuals involved until investigations are completed.
"The principles of justice and due process must be respected.
"This case is not merely about a pilot. It affects the credibility of the country's security system, the reputation of Malaysia's aviation industry and the confidence of the international community in the integrity of the nation's gateways," he said.
Jais said the integrity of a security system should be measured not by how it performs under normal conditions, but by its ability to prevent crime from breaching every layer of security.
"If weaknesses exist, they must be rectified immediately, transparently and without compromise," he said.

Title: Madani economy framework's biggest challenge now is stronger execution, not policy direction: Economist
Article:
BANGI: The Madani Economy framework has made progress in several key areas but stronger execution and better public reporting are needed to achieve its aspirations.
Malaysian Inclusive Development and Advancement Institute (Minda-UKM) director Prof Tan Sri Dr Noor Azlan Ghazali said the framework's biggest challenge is no longer its policy direction, but ensuring that implementation keeps pace with its ambitions.
"Looking more specifically, when the framework was launched, it outlined seven medium- and long-term aspirations under the Madani Economy.
"Three of the seven are progressing quite comfortably in terms of the fiscal deficit, women's labour force participation and the country's competitiveness.
"However, the other four have not failed, but they have not progressed as well," Azlan said after a Bicara Persada panel session.
The panel session was held as the Madani Economy framework marked three years since its launch by the government on July 27, 2023.
It outlined two main priorities: restructuring the economy to position the country as a leading economy in Asia and improving the quality of life for all Malaysians.
It is anchored on three key pillars: raising the ceiling, good governance and public sector reform, and raising the floor.
The framework sets out seven medium to long-term aspirations.
These include becoming one of the world's 30 largest economies, ranking among the top 12 globally in competitiveness, placing among the top 25 in the Corruption Perceptions Index, and increasing labour's share of income to 45 per cent.
The remaining aspirations are to rank among the top 25 in the Human Development Index, reduce the fiscal deficit to three per cent of gross domestic product or lower, and raise the female labour force participation rate to 60 per cent.
Malaysia is currently ranked above 50 in the Corruption Perceptions Index and above 60 in the Human Development Index.
Azlan said the framework was not off track, but required stronger implementation to achieve its targets.
He said greater clarity was needed on which government agencies were responsible for implementing specific initiatives under the framework, as well as how progress was being monitored and reported.
"At the moment, there is a lack of clarity regarding how the Madani Economy is being implemented. Which agencies are involved? There may be clarity, but it may not have been communicated to the public.
"This is important in today's world. It would be good if this information could be made available to the public so that we can all work together to make the Madani Economy a success," he added.

Title: Motac supports bringing international artists for Sepang F1 after-party
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry (Motac) will support efforts to bring international artists to Malaysia for the Formula 1 after-party, said its secretary-general Datuk Shaharuddin Abu Sohot.
He said that while such entertainment programmes are typically organised by the private sector, the ministry plays a role in supporting and promoting them.
"For artists, we do support bringing them to Malaysia, but most of these programmes are carried out by the private sector.
"We do encourage and help promote international programmes that come to our country," he told reporters on the sidelines of the 11th Malaysia Business Events Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.
He said the return of the F1 race is expected to benefit the national tourism sector.
He said teams and crews typically arrive up to a week in advance, contributing to the local economy through spending on accommodation, food and transport.
"The local economy will be boosted with F1 in our country.
"We will also organise several events to attract tourists, especially those coming for the F1 programme. In Kuala Lumpur and Sepang, we will hold programmes to attract more tourists to our country while they watch the race," he said.
The ministry has not set a specific projection for visitor numbers linked specifically to the race, but he expects overall tourist arrivals to rise as a result of the event.
The Sepang International Circuit is set to host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4.

Title: Malaysia's physical rice stocks sufficient for six months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The country's physical rice stocks remain stable and sufficient to meet domestic demand for at least six months, providing a buffer against potential geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, the Dewan Negara was told today.
Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the current inventory stands at 1.237 million tonnes, comprising 200,000 tonnes in national buffer stock and 1.037 million tonnes in commercial reserves.
"We maintain the physical rice buffer stock managed by Padiberas Nasional Bhd (Bernas), as well as commercial stocks that can last at least six months in the event of an impending global supply crisis," he said during Question Time.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Senator Datuk Dr Mohd Hatta Md Ramli regarding government readiness in maintaining staple food reserves during international crises.
Chan added that the supply control mechanism is supported by government subsidies to regulate local white rice prices, ensuring market stability when global commodity prices fluctuate.
On the target to achieve an 80 per cent self-sufficiency ratio (SSR) for rice by 2030, Chan said the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry is expanding the use of drought-resistant padi varieties to counter declining production trends and climate threats like El Nino.
"One way to address this issue is by expanding the use of drought-resistant padi varieties such as MR 380, MR 381 and MR 382. We also want to implement farm water management practices such as Alternate Wetting and Drying and System of Rice Intensification," he said.
He said the ministry is also executing a five-season rice cultivation project over two years across areas under the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) alongside irrigation system upgrades.
To alleviate rising input costs, Chan said the government has introduced short-term measures, including a temporary Sales and Service Tax exemption for agricultural fertilisers such as rock phosphate and magnesium sulphate from Jan 1, to Dec 31, next year.
Additionally, the padi ploughing incentive for the 2026 planting season has been raised from RM160 to RM300 per hectare, involving an extra RM40 million allocation benefiting nearly 200,000 farmers.

Title: Three Bangladeshis killed, one injured in suspected fight among co-workers
Article:
PORT DICKSON: Three Bangladeshi men were killed while another was seriously injured in what is believed to have been a fight among co-workers at a house in Taman Linggi here yesterday afternoon.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police also arrested a fellow Bangladeshi man in his 40s who is believed to be involved in the incident.
He said police received a report from members of the public at about 4.15pm yesterday about a fight involving several Bangladeshi nationals at the house.
"Acting on the information, a team from the Linggi police station rushed to the scene and arrested a Bangladeshi man in his 40s," he said in a statement today.
Alzafny said preliminary investigations later led police to the discovery of two more bodies at the Sua Manggis estate in Linggi.
"The three Bangladeshi men were confirmed dead after suffering severe injuries to various parts of their bodies, while another victim sustained injuries and is receiving treatment at Rembau Hospital," he said.
Initial investigations found that all those involved were co-workers who worked and lived at the same residence.
"The incident is believed to have occurred at several locations, and investigations are ongoing to establish the full sequence of events.
"Preliminary checks found that the suspect has no previous criminal record. He will be brought before the Port Dickson magistrate's court today for a remand application," he said.
Alzafny said the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, adding that the motive remains under investigation.

Title: Child sexual abuse cases in Selangor surge 70pc since 2021
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Child sexual abuse cases in Selangor have increased by 70 per cent since 2021, the state assembly was told today.
State Women Development and Social Welfare Committee chairman Anfaal Saari said the number of cases had risen consistently year-on-year, although the trend also reflected greater public awareness and willingness to report such crimes.
She said rape remained the most common sexual offence involving children, with 1,845 cases recorded between 2021 and 2025.
This was followed by physical abuse (1,654 cases), non-physical abuse (156), possession of child pornography (42), and producing or distributing child pornography (24).
"The most significant increase was recorded in physical sexual abuse, which rose by 70 per cent since 2021.
"While the upward trend is worrying, it also shows greater readiness among the public to come forward and report such cases," she said in reply to Mohd Shafie Ngah (PN-Sungai Ramal).
Anfaal, who is also the Templer assemblyman, said the state had introduced several intervention measures, including the Social and Reproductive Health Education Programme by the National Population and Family Development Board, anti-violence campaigns and grants to the Social Welfare Department to support peer-guidance advocacy in schools.
She said the state was also working with the Selangor Islamic Religious Department, the Selangor Association of Tahfiz Al-Quran Institutions and schools to expand awareness efforts.
"The programmes focus on educating children and students about safe touch practices and encouraging them to report concerns through school counsellors or the Talian Kasih 15999 helpline," she said.

Title: GFM wins RM83.1mil Pengerang contracts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Integrated facilities management services provider GFM Services Bhd has secured additional release orders worth RM83.1 million for major turnaround works at the Pengerang Integrated Complex (PIC) in Johor.
The contracts comprise RM16.3 million awarded to its wholly-owned subsidiary Highbase Strategic Sdn Bhd by Petronas Chemicals Isononanol Sdn Bhd and RM66.8 million awarded to its 60 per cent-owned indirect subsidiary Shapadu CR Asia Sdn Bhd by Pengerang Refining Company Sdn Bhd.
The release orders were secured under the company's existing integrated turnaround main mechanical and maintenance mechanical static (TA4MS) contract, with works scheduled to begin in 2027.
Including the RM148.2 million in release orders secured in July, GFM has accumulated turnaround work packages at PIC worth RM231.3 million.
PIC, which began operations in 2019, is preparing for its first major turnaround involving extensive maintenance, inspection and replacement works across the integrated downstream complex to ensure the continued reliability, safety and efficiency of its operations.
The latest awards expand the scope of work announced in July and are expected to contribute to the GFM's earnings for the year ending Dec 31, 2027.
Group managing director Ruslan Nordin said the latest contracts reflect the strength of GFM's expertise and complementary capabilities within its energy division.
"We will work closely with the project owners and stakeholders to deliver the awarded works safely, efficiently and in line with the required technical and operational standards," he said in a statement.
GFM's energy division comprises Highbase Strategic, 51 per cent-owned HIMS Integrated Services Sdn Bhd, a joint venture with Singapore-based Mun Siong Engineering Ltd, and 60 per cent-owned indirect subsidiary Shapadu CR Asia.
Collectively, these entities enable the group to deliver specialised mechanical maintenance and turnaround services across major downstream oil and gas facilities.

Title: Family of sisters killed in Klang crash considers legal action
Article:
KLANG: The family of two sisters killed in a fatal accident is considering legal action against the accused, the lawyer representing their interests said.
Watching brief lawyer Royston Tan said they were gathering the relevant documents and obtaining further instructions from the family with a view to pursuing appropriate civil claims and other available legal remedies.
Tan said this after mention proceedings for Ang Kim Lai, 75, who pleaded not guilty to a charge of reckless driving that allegedly caused the deaths of Wong Nyok Sim, 61, and Wong Nyoke Fong, 56.
The offence allegedly took place at 7.30pm on May 15 along Jalan Pekan Baru.
The charge under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act carries a jail term of between five and 10 years, a fine of RM20,000 to RM50,000, and suspension of the driving licence upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Salman Alfarisi Nawawi requested another mention date pending the post-mortem, pathology and chemist reports.
Magistrate A. Khartiyayini fixed Nov 5 for mention.
Ang was represented by lawyer Tong Kuan Ling.
Earlier, Ang arrived at the courtroom accompanied by a family member and appeared calm while waiting for proceedings to begin.
He was granted RM10,000 bail with one surety and had his driving licence suspended after being charged.
North Klang police chief Assistant Commissioner S. Vijaya Rao previously said a sport utility vehicle allegedly struck three pedestrians along Jalan Pekan Baru before fleeing the scene.
The suspect was later arrested at his restaurant. Police checks showed he had no previous criminal or narcotics record.
Nyoke Fong's 17-year-old son was injured in the incident.

Title: Toyota lifts annual forecast despite Q1 profit drop on weak China sales
Article:
TOKYO: Toyota on Tuesday raised its annual operating profit forecast by 13 per cent to reflect a weaker yen — the upward revision coming despite reporting a fifth consecutive quarterly earnings decrease on slumping sales in China.
The world's largest automaker now expects 3.4 trillion yen (US$21.6 billion) in operating profit for the current financial year to end-March, up from its previous forecast of three trillion yen.
"In addition to revised foreign exchange assumptions, we steadily accumulated improvements in our marketing efforts, including increased sales supported by the establishment of alternative logistics routes to the Middle East," Toyota said in a statement.
The upbeat revision and the announcement of a share buyback failed to boost its stock, with shares in the automaker dropping 2.3 per cent in afternoon trade.
Operating profit for the April-June first quarter declined nine per cent to 1.06 trillion yen, compared with a median forecast of 1.11 trillion yen in a poll of eight analysts surveyed by LSEG.
The revised annual profit outlook also did not take into account the impact of a deadly earthquake that struck Japan's Kyushu island last month, disrupting production at suppliers and forcing Toyota to halt output at four domestic plants.
Toyota said it plans to buy back shares worth up to one trillion yen, equivalent to as much as 4.22 per cent of outstanding stock. It also plans to cancel 200 million shares.
It raised its annual vehicle shipment target by 100,000 units to 9.7 million, citing solid demand in North America and Europe, among the few markets where Toyota reported sales growth during the April-June quarter.

Title: Toyota profit drops for fifth straight quarter on China slump, Iran war impact
Article:
TOKYO: Toyota said on Tuesday that profit fell for a fifth straight quarter, hurt by a slide in China sales as well as higher material and parts costs stemming from the Iran war.
Operating profit for the April-June first quarter declined nine per cent to 1.06 trillion yen (US$6.7 billion), compared with a median forecast of 1.11 trillion yen in a poll of eight analysts surveyed by LSEG.
But the world's largest automaker lifted its full-year profit outlook by 13 per cent to 3.4 trillion yen from 3.0 trillion yen.

Title: 2 who died in Japan mall explosion were told by employer to return inside
Article:
TOKYO: Two women who died in an explosion at an Aeon shopping mall in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan, had originally safely evacuated following a major earthquake but were ordered back inside to secure cash, Xinhua reported.
The operator of the variety store chain, Habita, on Monday admitted to having given the instruction.
The company had since apologised to the bereaved family members and handed over a written account of events.
After Tuesday's magnitude 7.1 earthquake, which registered up to 7, the highest level on Japan's seismic intensity scale, a massive explosion ripped through the Aeon Mall Kumamoto building in Kashima Town, killing seven people, including the two employees.
The two, including a 22-year-old woman, had initially evacuated the mall after the powerful quake, but were told to return inside to put cash in a safe.
Koji Yuse, 64, sales manager at Kumamoto-based Habita, told reporters on Monday afternoon that he had instructed the store manager to have the two employees reenter the building and move the day's sales proceeds from the store on the second floor to a safe on the first floor.
Yuse said, "I think the order was inappropriate. I deeply regret it."
The Kumamoto prefectural government said that as of Tuesday morning, 36 people had been confirmed dead as a direct result of the earthquake, with two other deaths still under investigation.

Title: Hartalega's Q1 earnings jump on higher prices, cost savings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hartalega Holdings Bhd's net profit surged to RM70 million in the first quarter ended June 30 2026 from RM12.6 million a year ago.
This was driven by higher average selling prices and sustained cost optimisation initiatives, according to a bourse filing.
The glovemaker's revenue grew 9.5 per cent to RM605.75 million from RM553 million.
Hartalega said it remains cautiously optimistic about the long-term outlook for the global glove industry.
This will be supported by heightened hygiene awareness as well as rising healthcare access in emerging markets and demand that continues to exceed pre-pandemic levels.
The company said the clearance of pandemic-era inventories resulted in healthier customer stock levels, although ordering patterns remain uneven, with the pace of recovery varying across different markets.
"Against this backdrop, the company delivered an improved performance during the quarter despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and challenging industry conditions.
"Stronger results were underpinned by higher ASPs, improved production efficiency, lower unit production costs and disciplined cost management, which together helped mitigate the impact of higher input costs and market volatility," it said.
Hartalega said near-term operating conditions are expected to remain challenging as continued uncertainty over US tariff policies reshapes global trade flows.
The company said while China's glove exports to the US have declined significantly, surplus production capacity has been diverted to non-US markets.
This intensified price competition and weighed on industry volumes and margins, particularly in Europe, Asia and other emerging markets.
"Heightened geopolitical tensions, particularly the ongoing Middle East conflict, add further uncertainty to energy markets and global supply chains, with potential knock-on effects on crude oil prices, nitrile butadiene rubber latex costs and logistics expenses.
"Raw material prices, foreign exchange movements, customer ordering patterns and supply chain conditions are expected to remain volatile," it said.
The company said it is managing these risks by diversifying its supplier base, maintaining flexible logistics and managing inventory prudently, while working closely with suppliers and customers to ensure a stable supply chain.
Despite challenges such as global overcapacity and intensifying competition from Chinese manufacturers, Hartalega said it is well positioned to weather near-term headwinds.
It expects continued investments in automation and technology, together with ongoing cost optimisation and operational efficiency improvements, to strengthen its competitiveness, improve resilience and support long-term margin growth.

Title: Hotel worker gets five years' jail, whipping for sexually assaulting fiancée's daughter
Article:
PASIR MAS: A hotel worker was sentenced to five years' jail and two strokes of the rotan by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to two counts of sexually assaulting his fiancée's 16-year-old daughter at a hotel in Tanah Merah last month.
The 34-year-old accused entered the guilty plea after the charges were read before judge Zulkpli Abdullah.
The accused was charged with sexually assaulting the teenager at 3am and 11am in a hotel room in Tanah Merah on July 24.
He was charged under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017 which carries a prison sentence of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Based on the facts of the case, the accused picked up the victim from her father's house in Kuala Krai under the pretext of arranging her school transfer to Besut, Terengganu.
Instead, he brought her to the hotel where he worked and molested her while she was asleep, telling her, "adik comel, papa sayang adik, adik kecil macam baby" (you are cute, papa loves you, you are small like a baby).
Following the incident, the victim fled the hotel and was spotted by members of the public, who brought her to the Tanah Merah district police headquarters.
Police subsequently contacted the victim's mother in Besut.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Aisyha Nai'lah Harizan appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was unrepresented.
Earlier, Siti Aisyha Nai'lah urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence as a deterrent given the gravity of the offence, noting that the accused betrayed the guardian's trust by taking advantage of the victim at the hotel.
In mitigation, the accused pleaded for a lenient sentence, stating he was the eldest of five siblings and needed to support his family.
Zulkpli sentenced the accused to five years' jail and one stroke of the cane for each charge, ordering the sentences to run concurrently.
The court also ordered the accused to undergo counselling while in prison and to serve two years under police supervision upon completion of his sentence.

Title: Radzi Rahimi remembered as a dedicated leader who inspired Maran youth, says Pahang MB
Article:
TEMERLOH: The tragic death of Maran Umno Youth chief Mohd Radzi Rahimi is a huge loss to the community in Maran, especially its youth, as he had devoted much of his time to serving the people.
Pahang Menteri Besar and Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail described Radzi as an approachable leader who was respected by people from all walks of life and remembered for his cheerful personality.
"His outstanding qualities and friendly personality made him easily approachable. I truly feel the loss as he was an easy-going person who connected well with everyone.
"As an Umno Youth leader, he worked hard and contributed greatly to the party. His passing is a major loss to the people of Maran, especially its youth," he told reporters after paying his last respects to Radzi at Paya Luas Mosque yesterday.
In the 12.30pm incident yesterday, Radzi, his wife Nuraini Mohammad Jafri, 36, their five-year-old son, Rizz Hazim, and Radzi's brother-in-law, Mohammad Nizam Mohammad Jafri, 34, were killed after a
large tree fell onto their pick-up truck
in Janda Baik. Rizz Hazim's twin brother, Muhammad Rizz Haziq, survived with injuries.
Meanwhile, Maran Umno division chief Datuk Seri Shahaniza Shamsuddin said she was very close to Radzi and knew the late leader was well-liked by people from all walks of life, especially the youth in Maran.
She said that until the end of his life, Radzi continued contributing to the community by organising various programmes for young people and was always surrounded by the youth.
"Radzi was seen as a future leader of Maran because he possessed well-rounded leadership qualities," she said.

Title: Op Kalidasa cripples syndicate, RM20.74 million in drugs seized
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Police have crippled a drug trafficking syndicate after seizing 409.4kg of methamphetamine and 900 MDMA-laced vape cartridges worth a combined RM20.74 million in Selangor.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said two local men, aged 24 and 26, were arrested in two raids under Op Kalidasa on July 29.
"The operation was launched following intelligence gathered by the department.
"The first raid was conducted at Batu 22, Mukim Ijok, along Jalan Kuala Selangor in Sungai Buloh," he told reporters here today.
He said police caught the two suspects while they were unloading sacks believed to contain drugs into two Proton X70 vehicles.
"The drugs had earlier been left in a bushy area near a temple, which was apparently used as a landmark," he said.
Hussein clarified that the drugs were not hidden within the temple grounds but in nearby bushes.
He said police seized 21 white plastic sacks containing 409 packages of crystalline chunks and powder believed to be methamphetamine.
The methamphetamine weighed 409.4kg.
Hussein said another syndicate had earlier delivered the consignment to the location before the two suspects arrived to collect it.
"Police are investigating where the suspects intended to transport the drugs.
"A follow-up raid was conducted at a rented house in Taman Putra Damai, Petaling Jaya, which was being used as a drug store," he said, adding that police seized 900 vape cartridges containing an estimated 1.8 litres of liquid believed to be MDMA.
He said the house had been rented for several months and was allegedly being used to store drug-laced vape cartridges pending distribution.
The two Proton X70 vehicles were used by the suspects to transport the drugs.
Hussein said the two men acted as transporters for the syndicate, which was believed to have been active since January.
"The drugs were estimated to be capable of supplying 2.04 million users.
"A preliminary urine test found the second suspect positive for THC," he said, adding that background checks revealed both suspects had criminal records. They were remanded for seven days from July 30 until Aug 5.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which carries the death penalty or life imprisonment, and no fewer than 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
Police are still investigating whether the syndicate had links to other drug networks previously dismantled by the authorities.
Hussein said numerous drug syndicates were operating independently and continuously looking for opportunities to transport and distribute narcotics.
Members of the public with information on drug-related activities may contact the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department hotline at 012-208 7222.
